data.name: Damaris
data.gender_notes: Damaris is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'damar', which means 'tame, subdue'. In the New Testament, Damaris is a woman who is converted to Christianity by Saint Paul. She is described as 'noted for her great virtues'. The name may reflect her tender and beloved nature. The name Damaris carries the meaning “Beloved, tender heart” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Damaris usually hope their child will grow to embody beloved, tender heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion, loyalty, and a gentle spirit.
data.etymology: Damaris belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Beloved, tender heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Damaris total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: דמריס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם דמריס מקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'עקרת בית' או 'אישה שקטה'. הוא מוזכר בברית החדשה, בספר מעשי השליחים, כאחת מהנשים שהאמינו במשיח ישוע. השם משמש כסמל לאישה מאמינה, שקטה ומרגיעה.

in_greek.name: Δαμάρις
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δαμάρις προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'δαμάζω', που σημαίνει 'καταπτοώ' ή 'ησυχάζω'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, συγκεκριμένα στο βιβλίο των Πράξεων των Αποστόλων, αναφέρεται ως μία από τις γυναίκες που πίστεψαν στον Ιησού Χριστό. Συμβολίζει τη γυναίκα που έχει ησυχία και γαλήνη στην καρδιά της.

in_latin.name: Damaris
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Damaris originem habet ex Graeco et significat 'mulier quieta' vel 'domus regina'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen hoc gerebatur ad mulieres credentes qui vitam quietam et contemplativam ducebant. Est etiam nomen quoddam biblicum, quod in Actibus Apostolorum invenitur.

in_english.name: Damaris
in_english.long_meaning: The name Damaris originates from the Greek word 'damazō', meaning 'to tame' or 'to calm'. It is mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in Acts 17:34, as one of the women who believed in Jesus Christ. The name symbolizes a woman of quiet strength, serenity, and domestic virtues. Historically, it has been used in Christian tradition to signify a woman of faith and inner peace. The name Damaris conveys a sense of calmness, peacefulness, and gentle strength.

data.cultural_impact: The name Damaris has been popular in Christian communities and cultures throughout history. It carries the implication of strength and conversion, as seen in the Biblical character, Damaris, who was known for her great virtues and was converted by Saint Paul. It is a testament to the impact of Christianity on the naming of children, and the legacy of strong, virtuous women.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Damaris has spiritual significance as it reminds us of the importance of conversion and the power of God to transform our lives. It also highlights the value of virtues such as tenderness, strength, and goodness, which are essential aspects of a godly character. This name encourages us to strive for spiritual growth and to emulate the virtues of Damaris and other saints who have gone before us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Damaris is derived from the Aramaic word 'dmar' meaning 'rebel' or 'disobedient'. In Christian tradition, St. Damaris is remembered for her conversion and unwavering faith during St. Paul's preaching in Athens. This name symbolizes the transformative power of faith and the possibility of redemption for even the most rebellious souls.

biblical_reference.note: Damaris is mentioned as one of the women who believed in Jesus Christ in Athens.

historical_references.reference: Damaris is mentioned in the New Testament as a woman who converted to Christianity after hearing the preaching of St. Paul.
